extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO (patent agents/attorneys, trademark agents), OED staff, and counsel handling USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing practitioner conduct before the USPTO: definitions of practice in patent and trademark matters, specific rules of professional conduct allegedly violated, requirements for an affidavit of resignation/exclusion on consent, and consequences for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice before the Office in patent matters (37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b)(1), practice of patent law before the USPTO includes, but is not limited to, preparing and prosecuting any patent application; consulting with or giving advice to a client in contemplation of filing a patent application or other document with the Office; drafting the specification or claims of a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is used to determine whether a person who is not authorized to practice patent law before the Office has nevertheless engaged in patent practice. The Final Order cites examples (preparing provisional and non-provisional applications; providing patent legal advice; filing responses to Office correspondence) as activities falling within this definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act with reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client. The OED alleged respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 by failing to timely respond to USPTO correspondence, resulting in client matters being abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order illustrates this violation with repeated failures to notify clients of Office actions and Notices of Abandonment and a pattern of abandoned trademark applications. Such neglect supports disciplinary action including exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably consult with client about means to accomplish objectives (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must reasonably consult with clients about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure examples in the Order include not informing clients of Office actions or advising on response options, and filing petitions to revive without consulting or informing clients about the petition and its possible consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep client reasonably informed about status of a matter (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners are required to keep clients reasonably informed about the status of their matters before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order documents a pattern of not notifying clients of Office actions, Notices of Abandonment, revivals, or petitions — conduct that violated this obligation and led to abandonment of client rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain matters sufficiently to permit informed client decisions (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must explain matters to the extent reasonably necessary to permit a client to make informed decisions regarding the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record shows respondents did not explain options for responding to Office actions or the potential consequences of non-response, thereby failing to enable informed client decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice of patent law before the USPTO (37 C.F.R. § 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in the unauthorized practice of law in patent matters before the USPTO is prohibited. A person not authorized to practice in patent matters must not prepare or prosecute patent applications or provide patent legal advice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states respondent, not a registered patent practitioner, prepared and filed provisional and non-provisional patent applications, represented applicants in 51 patent matters, responded to Office actions, and received compensation — conduct constituting unauthorized practice under § 11.5(b)(1) and prohibited by § 11.505 unless associated with a registered practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO is sanctionable under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED alleged that the respondent's pattern of neglect, failures to communicate, and unauthorized practice constituted conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice, supporting exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation / Exclusion on Consent requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit of resignation submitted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 must satisfy the regulatory requirements for approval of exclusion on consent (including that consent be freely and voluntarily rendered and awareness of pending disciplinary proceedings and consequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order approves the respondent's 15‑page Affidavit of Resignation under § 11.27(b) and notes the affidavit acknowledged voluntary consent, awareness of the Complaint, knowledge of relevant rules (§§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, 11.60), and acceptance of exclusion in trademark and non-patent matters. Approval triggers publication obligations and conditions on reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal recognition and its limits (37 C.F.R. § 11.14(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal recognition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(c) allows a foreign trademark agent limited authority to represent parties located in the agent's home country before the USPTO in trademark matters only, subject to compliance with the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order emphasizes that reciprocal recognition is limited in scope (trademark matters only) and obligates the foreign-recognized individual to comply with USPTO professional conduct rules; misuse beyond the limited scope (e.g., practicing patent law) violates the conditions of recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to designate and monitor contact information for Office correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: When a practitioner designates postal and electronic addresses in the Attorney Information section, the practitioner is responsible for receiving and acting on USPTO correspondence sent to those addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order recounts that Office communications were emailed/mailed to addresses that respondent had designated, but respondent failed to notify clients or act, and did not take reasonable steps to rectify alleged non-receipt — contributing to abandonment and disciplinary findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify clients about petitions to revive and their consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners who file petitions to revive abandoned applications must notify and advise their clients about the petition filings and potential consequences to the clients' intellectual property rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order criticizes filing petitions to revive without client knowledge or consent and failing to advise clients about the potential consequences of the grant or denial of such petitions; this conduct evidences failure to consult and keep clients informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for U.S. counsel for non-U.S. domiciliaries in trademark matters (37 C.F.R. § 2.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: As amended effective Aug. 3, 2019 (84 Fed. Reg. 31498), 37 C.F.R. § 2.11 requires non-U.S. domiciled trademark applicants to have U.S. counsel; this interacts with and affected 37 C.F.R. § 11.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes the rule change and places it in context as part of the Office's governance of foreign-recognized practitioners; practitioners must be aware of and comply with this requirement when representing foreign parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and conditions of exclusion on consent and reinstatement presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An exclusion on consent is effective when approved; the respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during the exclusion and § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement. The OED Director will conclusively presume allegations in the Complaint are true and that the respondent could not have successfully defended against them for the purpose of evaluating reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explains that although the respondent did not admit violating the Rules, he acknowledged that, for reinstatement purposes, the OED will treat the Complaint allegations as true and unrefuted; reinstatement will be subject to compliance with specified regulations and any conditions imposed by the Office.
